steps.en: What you see: One territory stops thickening while the rest compensates with vigorous motion. Fresh infarction shows hypokinesis or akinesis with normal wall thickness. Old infarction shows a thin bright scar that never thickens. Ejection fraction falls in proportion to the number of segments involved, and an apical aneurysm may balloon outward in systole.

Normal values with units: Ejection fraction after infarction. Normal about 55 percent or more. Each additional akinetic territory lowers it further, and below 40 percent marks significant dysfunction.. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left ventricular ejection fraction

Wall motion score index. Total segment scores divided by segments seen. Normal equals 1.0 and higher values mark a larger infarct burden.. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on regional function and segmentation

Left ventricular wall thickness in scar. Normal diastolic thickness about 6 to 10 mm. Thinned bright walls below this range mark old scar.. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left ventricular wall thickness

ECG and heart sound correlation ecg: ST elevation with Q waves marks the infarct territory with reciprocal ST depression in opposite leads. New left bundle branch block can mask an anterior occlusion. Always read the ECG before the echo in chest pain.

ECG and heart sound correlation sounds: A fourth sound marks acute ischaemia and a third sound marks extensive dysfunction. A new pansystolic murmur warns of papillary muscle rupture or septal rupture.

What to report: Each abnormal segment with its territory and grade of dysfunction
Ejection fraction with the method and the wall motion score index
Thrombus, aneurysm, effusion or mechanical complication with sizes
Comparison with any old study to separate new from old disease
Red flags needing urgent referral: New severe regurgitation or septal rupture with shock, needs emergency surgical review
Large anterior akinesis with visible thrombus, needs urgent anticoagulation review
Ongoing chest pain with new wall motion abnormality, needs immediate reperfusion pathway activation
Pitfalls: Stunning recovers over days, so a single early study overreads final infarct size.
Left bundle branch block dyssynchrony mimics septal infarction, so check QRS width first.
Takotsubo balloons the apex beyond one territory with clean coronaries, so keep an open mind in stress contexts.

todo.en: How to get it on the probe, step by step: Start in the apical four chamber view and watch every segment thicken inward in systole.
Move through two chamber and long axis views so all 17 segments are seen.
Score each segment as normal, hypokinetic, akinetic or dyskinetic on one frozen loop per view.
Measure ejection fraction by Simpson biplane and compare with the segment burden.
Check for thrombus in the apex, papillary muscle rupture and septal rupture as mechanical complications.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Calling foreshortening an apical infarct. Fix: Slide down until the apex is longest and thinnest. A cut apex fakes an apical wall motion defect.
Calling tethered passive motion true hypokinesis. Fix: Watch two full cycles and judge thickening, not just motion, since tethered normal tissue still moves.
Calling lateral dropout an old scar. Fix: Turn lateral gain down and rescan. Dropout mimics scar in the anterior wall.

remember.en: Spot mechanical complications and activate the right urgent pathway.

q.en: What defines true hypokinesis against passive tethering?

why.en: Judge thickening, not excursion. Tethered normal tissue moves but still thickens.

q.en: Which pattern marks a large completed infarct?

o.en: Small localised hypokinesis of one territory
Akinesis with aneurysm formation across many segments

why.en: More than 6 abnormal segments, or akinesis with aneurysm formation, marks large disease.

q.en: Ongoing chest pain shows a new extensive wall motion abnormality. What next?

o.en: Immediate reperfusion pathway with ECG correlation

why.en: New wall motion abnormality with ischaemic pain is an emergency for the reperfusion pathway.

q.en: Which complications must every post infarct study exclude?

o.en: Papillary muscle rupture, septal rupture and apical thrombus

why.en: Papillary rupture, septal rupture and apical thrombus change management within hours.
